updates.title: Tech View offers List's columns plus Assigned Techs in its own Columns menu
preconditions: You are signed in as an Owner or Admin user whose role has Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit, at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919).
Your browser window is at least 1024 px wide, so the display switcher (List, Tech View, Board View) shows at the right of the Work Orders toolbar.
Technician {Technician-A} (for example Esther Howard) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.

Approved work order {Work-order-1} (for example S10043-17601) for customer {Customer-A} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST F2 Tech Columns") is led by {Technician-A} and has one approved line, {Line-1} (for example "Service - Full grease service").
In Tech View's Column Selection, Assigned Techs is on, and On Site, VIN/Serial # and Lead Technician are off, as they start for a new user.
steps: Open Work Orders and click the All tab.
Type the name of {Customer-A} in Search.
Click List in the display switcher at the right of the toolbar.
Click the Column Selection button (tooltip "Column Selection") and write down every column name in the menu.
Close the menu.
Click Tech View in the display switcher (tooltip "Tech View").
Click the Column Selection button and write down every column name in the menu, and which ones are on.
Turn On Site on.
Turn VIN/Serial # on.
Turn Lead Technician on.
Close the menu and read the Tech View column headers.
Click the Column Selection button.
Turn Assigned Techs off.
Close the menu and read the Tech View column headers.
Click the Column Selection button, turn Assigned Techs on and close the menu.
Read the Tech View column headers.
results: Step 4: List's menu does not offer Assigned Techs.
Steps 6 and 7: Tech View has its own Column Selection button, which opens Tech View's own column menu.
Step 7: every column offered in List's menu is also offered in Tech View's menu, and Tech View's menu also offers Assigned Techs, which is on.
Step 11: On Site, VIN/Serial # and Lead Technician each show as a column in the Tech View table.
Step 14: the Assigned Techs column no longer shows in Tech View.
Step 16: the Assigned Techs column shows in Tech View again.

doc_part1: Sign in as an Owner or Admin user. On a QA site click the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page; you appear as "Admin ShopView". To check the permissions: your initials (top right) > Settings > Roles & Permissions > Admin > Work orders: View and Create & Edit are on.

Pick one location for the whole case; it is shown in the top bar next to the bell (to change it: your initials > Change Location). This is {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919). Create everything below at {Location-A}.
Use a desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide (narrower windows show only the List, with no display switcher).

Your initials > Settings > Staff. Reuse a staff member only if they are active, have Time Clock on, {Location-A} in Location and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User. Otherwise click New Staff Member and enter First Name and Last Name (for example Esther Howard), an Email, Role Technician, at least one Department (required), Location {Location-A}, turn Time Clock on, then Save & Close. This is {Technician-A}.

Top menu Customers > New Customer > Name (for example "ZZAUTOTEST F2 Tech Columns") > Save. This is {Customer-A}; use it for this case only. On the customer page click Contacts > New Contact > First Name and Last Name (for example ZZAUTOTEST Contact) > Save. Then Assets > New Asset > pick the contact, Year (for example 2022), Make (type "Freight" and pick Freightliner), Model (for example M2), Unit (for example TRK-118) > Save. Contact and Make are required.

Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick {Customer-A} and its asset > Save (if a Confirmation about the credit limit appears, click Create). The work order opens on its Lines tab with the New Line form. In What Are You Doing? type "grease" and pick the ready-made line "Service - Full grease service", turn Line Approved on and click Save & Close. The status reads Approved. Write down the number shown at the top left (for example S10043-17601). This is {Work-order-1}. Its line is {Line-1}.
On {Work-order-1}'s page pick {Technician-A} in the Lead Technician dropdown; it saves at once (the dropdown shows once the work order is Approved).
Work Orders > All > click Tech View in the display switcher > Column Selection: turn Assigned Techs on and turn On Site, VIN/Serial # and Lead Technician off. Close the menu.

Check the setup worked: Work Orders > All > Search the name of {Customer-A}: {Work-order-1} shows with Lead Technician {Technician-A}. In Tech View the Assigned Techs column shows and On Site, VIN/Serial # and Lead Technician do not.
doc_part2: Goal: one Approved work order {Work-order-1} led by {Technician-A}, then compare List's and Tech View's column menus and turn columns on and off in Tech View.
Create {Customer-A}, {Work-order-1} and the lead on screen as in Part 1 and record {Work-order-1}.

Read both column menus with Playwright as exact strings (the List column selector has data-test-id button_column_selection; the Tech View one is UNVERIFIED: record its selector). Compare the two lists as sets: Tech View's must be List's plus Assigned Techs.

List's saved state (columns, filters, tab, sort) is the user preference GET/PUT /api/users/me/preferences/work-orders-list (playbook, Work Orders filters section); filter state persists on the server across browser contexts. The preference keys for Tech View's columns and Board View's fields are UNVERIFIED: record them from the network requests when you change a column.
Cleanup: after the case, turn On Site, VIN/Serial # and Lead Technician off again in Tech View and leave Assigned Techs on, so the user is back at the new-user starting columns for the next case.
Evidence: a screenshot after each step that has an expected result, the build marker, and the real value of every brace name.

quotes: Feature Overview
The existing filter views (the tabs on the left — All, Work Orders, Estimates, Completed) and the filter bar (search, status, assigned to me, and so on) apply the same way in every display option.
Feature Overview (the two exceptions)
Imported work orders are one exception: they open in List only (S1-R13a, S1-R13b). The Technician filter is the other: Tech View and Board View offer it and List does not (S1-R15).
Key Decisions
Permissions. Work Orders view permits viewing all four filter tabs and reordering technician groups/columns.
doc_part1: Sign in as an Owner or Admin user. On a QA site click the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page; you appear as "Admin ShopView". To check the permissions: your initials (top right) > Settings > Roles & Permissions > Admin > Work orders: View and Create & Edit are on.

Pick one location for the whole case; it is shown in the top bar next to the bell (to change it: your initials > Change Location). This is {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919). Create everything below at {Location-A}.
Use a desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide (narrower windows show only the List, with no display switcher).

Your initials > Settings > Staff. Reuse a staff member only if they are active, have Time Clock on, {Location-A} in Location and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User. Otherwise click New Staff Member and enter First Name and Last Name (for example Esther Howard), an Email, Role Technician, at least one Department (required), Location {Location-A}, turn Time Clock on, then Save & Close. This is {Technician-A}.

Top menu Customers > New Customer > Name (for example "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Tabs") > Save. This is {Customer-A}; use it for this case only. On the customer page click Contacts > New Contact > First Name and Last Name (for example ZZAUTOTEST Contact) > Save. Then Assets > New Asset > pick the contact, Year (for example 2022), Make (type "Freight" and pick Freightliner), Model (for example M2), Unit (for example TRK-118) > Save. Contact and Make are required.

Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick {Customer-A} and its asset > Save (if a Confirmation about the credit limit appears, click Create). The work order opens on its Lines tab with the New Line form. In What Are You Doing? type "grease" and pick the ready-made line "Service - Full grease service" and click Save & Close. Write down the number shown at the top left (for example S10043-17616). This is {Work-order-1}. It stays in Estimate. While it is an Estimate its Lead Technician is read-only on the work order page, so give it its lead from Board View: Work Orders > All > Board View > the card's More actions (…) > Reassign lead technician > pick {Technician-A} > Reassign.

Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick {Customer-A} and its asset > Save (if a Confirmation about the credit limit appears, click Create). The work order opens on its Lines tab with the New Line form. In What Are You Doing? type "grease" and pick the ready-made line "Service - Full grease service", turn Line Approved on and click Save & Close. The status reads Approved. Write down the number shown at the top left (for example S10043-17617). This is {Work-order-2}.
On {Work-order-2}'s page pick {Technician-A} in the Lead Technician dropdown; it saves at once (the dropdown shows once the work order is Approved).

Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick {Customer-A} and its asset > Save (if a Confirmation about the credit limit appears, click Create). The work order opens on its Lines tab with the New Line form. In What Are You Doing? type "grease" and pick the ready-made line "Service - Full grease service", turn Line Approved on and click Save & Close. The status reads Approved. Write down the number shown at the top left (for example S10043-17618). This is {Work-order-3}. On {Work-order-3}'s page pick {Technician-A} in the Lead Technician dropdown; it saves at once (the dropdown shows once the work order is Approved). Then move it to Complete with the status control on the work order page.
Work Orders > All: clear any Status selection (Clear selection) and turn Assigned to me off.

Check the setup worked: Work Orders > All > Search the name of {Customer-A} shows exactly {Work-order-1} (Estimate), {Work-order-2} (Approved) and {Work-order-3} (Complete), each with lead {Technician-A}. If a status or lead is wrong, fix it on the work order page (or from Board View for the Estimate) before starting.

quotes: In Tech View and Board View the filter bar also offers a Technician filter, after Assigned to me. It is a multi-select listing Unassigned first, then the location’s technicians (the same people who get a group or column, S9-R4), by first name then last name. Choosing one or more shows only those technicians’ groups or columns; every other group or column, pinned ones included, is hidden. It filters by lead technician only.
Feature Overview (the two exceptions)
Imported work orders are one exception: they open in List only (S1-R13a, S1-R13b). The Technician filter is the other: Tech View and Board View offer it and List does not (S1-R15).
Out of Scope

A Department filter. The design shows one, but a work order’s department is not shown or editable on any work order screen today, so users could not see why a work order matches. Revisit once the work order shows its department.
Out of Scope
The Customer and Service Advisor filter chips production retired in the redesign (SV-8785) are not brought back.
S1-R15b

List does not offer the Technician filter and stays as in production. Switching to List while technicians are chosen shows List as if none were chosen; switching back to Tech View or Board View brings the choice back. The choice is remembered the same way as the other filters.
